papers.title_en: OpenMQPI: An MLIR-based Pipeline to Offload Quantum Circuits via OpenMP
papers.authors: Ercüment Kaya, Ekin Devim Şahinkaya, Minh Chung, Martin Schulz
papers.evidence: 基于MLIR及自定义方言的硬件后端卸载流水线
papers.tldr: 量子软件栈与硬件后端紧耦合，导致HPCQC应用难以复用和集成量子加速器。OpenMQPI基于MLIR扩展OpenMP，引入QPIR方言表示target区域内的量子线路，并通过编译流水线与运行时MQSS插件实现量子线路卸载。在VQE、QFT和Deutsch-Jozsa上测试5至20量子比特，20比特VQE耗时5.18秒，低于Qiskit的5.83秒和CUDA Quantum的7.39秒。该工作为HPC应用接入量子资源提供了标准化卸载路径。
papers.abstract_en: Quantum computing introduces specialized software stacks and programming interfaces that are often tightly coupled to specific ecosystems and hardware backends, limiting interoperability and software reuse. For HPCQC application developers, this complicates the integration of quantum accelerators into existing applications. Existing quantum frameworks also use ecosystem-specific circuit representations and compilation pipelines, hindering integration with established heterogeneous compiler infrastructures. We propose OpenMQPI, an MLIR-based OpenMP extension for quantum programming that leverages OpenMP's standardized target offloading infrastructure to integrate quantum resources into HPC applications. OpenMQPI introduces QPIR, a lightweight MLIR dialect for representing quantum circuits within OpenMP target regions, and a compiler pipeline that performs quantum-specific optimizations and lowers circuits to executables compatible with OpenMP offloading. At runtime, an MQSS plugin enables the generated executable to offload quantum circuits to quantum hardware through the OpenMP target offloading model. We evaluate OpenMQPI using the VQE, QFT, and Deutsch-Jozsa algorithms with 5, 10, 15, and 20 qubits, comparing execution times against Qiskit and CUDA Quantum. OpenMQPI achieves the lowest average VQE execution time across all tested qubit configurations. At 20 qubits, it requires 5.18 s, compared with 5.83 s for Qiskit and 7.39 s for CUDA Quantum. For QFT and Deutsch-Jozsa, OpenMQPI achieves execution times comparable to Qiskit and lower than those of CUDA Quantum.

papers.title_en: EdgeKernelBench: Unified LLM-Driven Kernel Generation for Edge Backends
papers.authors: Yuhua Zheng, Xueyi Chen, Xinze Zou, Xin Li, Haoji Hu, Huan Wang
papers.evidence: 统一 IR 经编译器接口对接边缘后端
papers.tldr: 边缘部署面临硬件异构、软件栈碎片化和资源预算紧等挑战，LLM跨边缘后端的kernel生成尚缺系统研究。作者提出EdgeKernelBench，以统一IR连接各后端，并构建从单算子到紧凑模型图的分层基准，用TVM作参考编译器在异构边缘后端验证。单次生成最佳模型Correct@1为64.5%，但Fast@1.0仅25.5%，表明正确性未必转化为性能。为此提出分层IR优化的LEKA，在评测子集上Fast@1.0达43.5%，优于直接生成的13.0%和Claude Code的26.1%。
papers.abstract_en: Recent works show that LLMs can generate kernels with strong performance on server GPUs. Edge deployment presents distinct challenges because the hardware is heterogeneous, the software stacks are fragmented, and the resource budgets are tight. LLM kernel generation across diverse edge backends has yet to be studied systematically. We introduce EdgeKernelBench, which combines a unified IR deployment framework with a hierarchical benchmark for edge workloads. The unified IR captures reusable computation, scheduling, and memory decisions and connects to each target backend through a compiler interface. The benchmark spans progressively larger program scopes, from individual operators to compact model graphs, across representative edge application domains. We instantiate the design with TVM as a reference compiler and validate it across heterogeneous edge backends. With a single generation attempt, the best model achieves 64.5% Correct@1 but only 25.5% Fast@1.0. This gap shows that functional correctness does not consistently translate into performance gains. We therefore introduce the Layered Edge Kernel Agent (LEKA), which organizes optimization through a layered IR. On the agent evaluation subset, LEKA achieves 43.5% Fast@1.0, compared with 13.0% for direct generation and 26.1% for Claude Code. LEKA and Claude Code use the same base model and optimization budget. Together, EdgeKernelBench and LEKA support unified evaluation and layered optimization of kernels generated by LLMs across edge backends.
